sanskrit: susaṃrabdhaṃ tu saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ krodhamūrchitam rāmas tu parisāntvyātha vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Then Rāma, having gently calmed Lakṣmaṇa the son of Sumitrā who was enraged and overcome with fury, spoke these words.

sanskrit: kim atra dhanuṣā kāryam asinā vā sacarmaṇā maheṣvāse mahāprājñe bharate svayam āgate
english: What use here is a bow, or a sword with its shield, now that Bharata himself—that great archer, that supremely wise one—has come in person?

sanskrit: prāptakālaṃ yad eṣo 'smān bharato draṣṭum icchati asmāsu manasāpy eṣa nāhitaṃ kiṃ cid ācaret
english: It is only fitting that Bharata wishes to see us now; he would not commit even in his mind any harm against us.

sanskrit: vipriyaṃ kṛtapūrvaṃ te bharatena kadā na kim īdṛśaṃ vā bhayaṃ te 'dya bharataṃ yo 'tra śaṅkase
english: Has Bharata ever done anything displeasing to you before? What manner of fear is it that you now suspect in Bharata?

sanskrit: na hi te niṣṭhuraṃ vācyo bharato nāpriyaṃ vacaḥ ahaṃ hy apriyam uktaḥ syāṃ bharatasyāpriye kṛte
english: You must not speak any harsh or unpleasant word to Bharata; for if harm were done to Bharata, I myself would be the one spoken ill of.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu putrāḥ pitaraṃ hanyuḥ kasyāṃ cid āpadi bhrātā vā bhrātaraṃ hanyāt saumitre prāṇam ātmanaḥ
english: How could sons slay their own father in any adversity? Or how could a brother slay his brother, O son of Sumitrā—a brother who is one's own very life?

sanskrit: yadi rājyasya hetos tvam imāṃ vācaṃ prabhāṣase vakṣyāmi bharataṃ dṛṣṭvā rājyam asmai pradīyatām
english: If you speak these words on account of the kingdom, then upon meeting Bharata I shall say to him: let the kingdom be given to him.

sanskrit: ucyamāno hi bharato mayā lakṣmaṇa tattvataḥ rājyam asmai prayaccheti bāḍham ity eva vakṣyati
english: For Bharata, O Lakṣmaṇa, when truly told by me 'give him the kingdom,' will respond with nothing but 'so be it.'

sanskrit: tathokto dharmaśīlena bhrātrā tasya hite rataḥ lakṣmaṇaḥ praviveśeva svāni gātrāṇi lajjayā
english: Thus addressed by his brother of righteous character, who was ever devoted to his welfare, Lakṣmaṇa seemed to shrink into his own body with shame.

sanskrit: vrīḍitaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca ha eṣa manye mahābāhur ihāsmān draṣṭum āgataḥ
english: Seeing Lakṣmaṇa abashed, the Rāghava spoke again: "I think that mighty-armed one comes here to see us."

sanskrit: vanavāsam anudhyāya gṛhāya pratineṣyati imāṃ vāpy eśa vaidehīm atyantasukhasevinīm
english: Reflecting on our forest-dwelling, he will take us back to the city—or at least this daughter of Videha who is accustomed to every comfort.

sanskrit: etau tau saṃprakāśete gotravantau manoramau vāyuvegasamau vīra javanau turagottamau
english: Those two noble horses shine forth, charming, swift as the wind, O hero—the finest of steeds.

sanskrit: sa eṣa sumahākāyaḥ kampate vāhinīmukhe nāgaḥ śatruṃjayo nāma vṛddhas tātasya dhīmataḥ
english: That very large elephant named Śatruṃjaya—the aged and wise one belonging to our father—trembles at the head of the army.

sanskrit: avatīrya tu sālāgrāt tasmāt sa samitiṃjayaḥ lakṣmaṇaḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā tasthau rāmasya pārśvataḥ
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, that conqueror of battles, having descended from the treetop of the sāla tree, stood at Rāma's side with palms joined in reverence.

sanskrit: bharatenātha saṃdiṣṭā saṃmardo na bhaved iti samantāt tasya śailasya senāvāsam akalpayat
english: Then, directed by Bharata so that there be no overcrowding, they arranged the camp of the army all around that mountain.

sanskrit: adhyardham ikṣvākucamūr yojanaṃ parvatasya sā pārśve nyaviśad āvṛtya gajavājirathākulā
english: The army of the Ikṣvākus, crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots, encamped on the flank of the mountain, covering a space of one and a half yojanas.

sanskrit: sā citrakūṭe bharatena senā dharmaṃ puraskṛtya vidhūya darpam prasādanārthaṃ raghunandanasya virocate nītimatā praṇītā
english: That army at Citrakūṭa, led by Bharata with righteousness foremost and pride cast aside, shone forth, guided by the wise one for the purpose of propitiating the son of Raghu.

sanskrit: niveśya senāṃ tu vibhuḥ padbhyāṃ pādavatāṃ varaḥ abhigantuṃ sa kākutstham iyeṣa guruvartakam
english: Having settled the army, that lord, finest among those who travel on foot, desired to go on foot to meet Kākutstha in the manner becoming toward an elder.

sanskrit: niviṣṭa mātre sainye tu yathoddeśaṃ vinītavat bharato bhrātaraṃ vākyaṃ śatrughnam idam abravīt
english: As soon as the army had settled in its proper position in an orderly manner, Bharata spoke these words to his brother Śatrughna.

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ vanam idaṃ saumya narasaṃghaiḥ samantataḥ lubdhaiś ca sahitair ebhis tvam anveṣitum arhasi
english: "Quickly, O gentle one, together with these groups of men and hunters, you should search this forest all around."

sanskrit: yāvan na rāmaṃ drakṣyāmi lakṣmaṇaṃ vā mahābalam vaidehīṃ vā mahābhāgāṃ na me śāntir bhaviṣyati
english: "Until I see Rāma, or mighty Lakṣmaṇa, or the illustrious Vaidehī, there will be no peace for me."

sanskrit: yāvan na candrasaṃkāśaṃ drakṣyāmi śubham ānanam bhrātuḥ padmapalāśākṣaṃ na me śāntir bhaviṣyati
english: "Until I behold my brother's auspicious face, moon-like, with eyes like lotus petals, there will be no peace for me."

sanskrit: yāvan na caraṇau bhrātuḥ pārthiva vyañjanānvitau śirasā dhārayiṣyāmi na me śāntir bhaviṣyati
english: "Until I bear on my head my brother's feet—marked with royal auspicious signs—there will be no peace for me."

sanskrit: yāvan na rājye rājyārhaḥ pitṛpaitāmahe sthitaḥ abhiṣekajalaklinno na me śāntir bhaviṣyati
english: "Until he who deserves kingship is established in the ancestral kingdom, drenched with the waters of consecration, there will be no peace for me."

sanskrit: kṛtakṛtyā mahābhāgā vaidehī janakātmajā bhartāraṃ sāgarāntāyāḥ pṛthivyā yānugacchati
english: "Fulfilled in purpose is that illustrious daughter of Janaka, Vaidehī, who follows her husband, lord of the earth bounded by the ocean."

sanskrit: subhagaś citrakūṭo 'sau girirājopamo giriḥ yasmin vasati kākutsthaḥ kubera ivanandane
english: "Blessed is that Citrakūṭa, that mountain resembling the king of mountains, in which Kākutstha dwells like Kubera in the Nandana grove."

sanskrit: kṛtakāryam idaṃ durgaṃ vanaṃ vyālaniṣevitam yad adhyāste mahātejā rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: "That inaccessible forest, frequented by wild beasts, has accomplished its purpose, for in it resides Rāma of great splendor, finest among those who bear weapons."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejā bharataḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ padbhyām eva mahātejāḥ praviveśa mahad vanam
english: Having spoken thus, Bharata of great splendor, that bull among men, entered the great forest on foot alone.

sanskrit: sa tāni drumajālāni jātāni girisānuṣu puṣpitāgrāṇi madhyena jagāma vadatāṃ varaḥ
english: He, the foremost among speakers, passed through the midst of those thickets of trees grown on the mountain slopes with their flower-laden tips.

sanskrit: sa gireś citrakūṭasya sālam āsādya puṣpitam rāmāśramagatasyāgner dadarśa dhvajam ucchritam
english: He approached a flowering sāla tree on Mount Citrakūṭa and saw the pillar of smoke rising from the fire that belonged to Rāma's hermitage.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bharataḥ śrīmān mumoda sahabāndhavaḥ atra rāma iti jñātvā gataḥ pāram ivāmbhasaḥ
english: Seeing it, the illustrious Bharata rejoiced together with his kinsmen, knowing "Rāma is here"—as if he had crossed to the far shore of the waters.

sanskrit: sa citrakūṭe tu girau niśāmya rāmāśramaṃ puṇyajanopapannam guhena sārdhaṃ tvarito jagāma punar niveśyaiva camūṃ mahātmā
english: Having spotted Rāma's sacred hermitage on Mount Citrakūṭa, that great-souled one, after settling the army once more, swiftly went forward together with Guha.

sanskrit: niviṣṭāyāṃ tu senāyām utsuko bharatas tadā jagāma bhrātaraṃ draṣṭuṃ śatrughnam anudarśayan
english: Once the army had encamped, the eager Bharata then went to see his brother, pointing the way to Śatrughna.

sanskrit: ṛṣiṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ saṃdiśya mātṝr me śīghram ānaya iti taritam agre sa jāgama guruvatsalaḥ
english: Having instructed the seer Vasiṣṭha—"Bring my mothers quickly"—he who was devoted to his elders hastened on ahead.

sanskrit: sumantras tv api śatughnam adūrād anvapadyata rāmadārśanajas tarṣo bharatasyeva tasya ca
english: Sumantra too followed close behind Śatrughna, for his longing to behold Rāma was just as great as Bharata's own.

sanskrit: gacchann evātha bharatas tāpasālayasaṃsthitām bhrātuḥ parṇakuṭīṃ śrīmān uṭajaṃ ca dadarśa ha
english: While walking, the illustrious Bharata then beheld his brother's leaf-hut standing in that ascetics' abode, and also the cottage.

sanskrit: śālāyās tv agratas tasyā dadarśa bharatas tadā kāṣṭāni cāvabhagnāni puṣpāṇy avacitāni ca
english: Before that shelter Bharata then saw broken pieces of firewood and flowers that had been gathered.

sanskrit: dadarśa ca vane tasmin mahataḥ saṃcayān kṛtān mṛgāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca karīṣaiḥ śītakāraṇāt
english: He also saw in that forest large heaps gathered of dried dung of deer and buffalo, stored against the cold.

sanskrit: gacchan eva mahābāhur dyutimān bharatas tadā śatrughnaṃ cābravīd dhṛṣṭas tān amātyāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Even while walking, the mighty-armed and radiant Bharata spoke joyfully to Śatrughna and to all those ministers.

sanskrit: manye prāptāḥ sma taṃ deśaṃ bharadvājo yam abravīt nātidūre hi manye 'haṃ nadīṃ mandākinīm itaḥ
english: "I believe we have reached the place that Bharadvāja described; I think the river Mandākinī is not too far from here."

sanskrit: uccair baddhāni cīrāṇi lakṣmaṇena bhaved ayam abhijñānakṛtaḥ panthā vikāle gantum icchatā
english: "These strips of bark cloth tied high up—this must be a marked path made by Lakṣmaṇa who desired to travel in the dark hours."

sanskrit: idaṃ codāttadantānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām śailapārśve parikrāntam anyonyam abhigarjatām
english: "And here, on the mountain's flank, are the tracks of swift elephants with prominent tusks, that have roamed about trumpeting at one another."

sanskrit: yam evādhātum icchanti tāpasāḥ satataṃ vane tasyāsau dṛśyate dhūmaḥ saṃkulaḥ kṛṣṭavartmanaḥ
english: "That smoke which the ascetics in the forest ever seek to kindle—look, there it rises densely along the well-worn path."

sanskrit: atrāhaṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ gurusatkārakāriṇam āryaṃ drakṣyāmi saṃhṛṣṭo maharṣim iva rāghavam
english: "Here I shall joyfully behold that tiger among men, that noble one who always honours his elders—Rāghava, like a great seer."

sanskrit: atha gatvā muhūrtaṃ tu citrakūṭaṃ sa rāghavaḥ mandākinīm anuprāptas taṃ janaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Then, having walked a short while, that Rāghava reached Citrakūṭa and came to the Mandākinī, and spoke these words to the people.

sanskrit: jagatyāṃ puruṣavyāghra āste vīrāsane rataḥ janendro nirjanaṃ prāpya dhin me janma sajīvitam
english: "That tiger among men who delights in the seat of heroes dwells on the ground; that lord of men has come to a desolate place—cursed be my birth and my very life!"

sanskrit: matkṛte vyasanaṃ prāpto lokanātho mahādyutiḥ sarān kāmān parityajya vane vasati rāghavaḥ
english: "On my account has the lord of the world, great in glory, fallen into calamity; relinquishing every pleasure, Rāghava dwells in the forest."

sanskrit: iti lokasamākruṣṭaḥ pādeṣv adya prasādayan rāmasya nipatiṣyāmi sītāyāś ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: "Condemned thus by all the world, today, seeking to appease them, I shall fall again and again at the feet of Rāma and Sītā."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa vilapaṃs tasmin vane daśarathātmajaḥ dadarśa mahatīṃ puṇyāṃ parṇaśālāṃ manoramām
english: So lamenting in that forest, the son of Daśaratha then saw the great, holy, and beautiful leaf-cottage.

sanskrit: sālatālāśvakarṇānāṃ parṇair bahubhir āvṛtām viśālāṃ mṛdubhis tīrṇāṃ kuśair vedim ivādhvare
english: Covered with the many leaves of sāla, tāla, and aśvakarṇa trees, broad and spread with soft kuśa grass like a sacrificial altar at a ceremony.

sanskrit: śakrāyudha nikāśaiś ca kārmukair bhārasādhanaiḥ rukmapṛṣṭhair mahāsāraiḥ śobhitāṃ śatrubādhakaiḥ
english: Adorned with bows resembling Indra's rainbow, massive and heavy, with golden backs, of great substance, capable of afflicting enemies.

sanskrit: arkaraśmipratīkāśair ghorais tūṇīgataiḥ śaraiḥ śobhitāṃ dīptavadanaiḥ sarpair bhogavatīm iva
english: Graced by terrible arrows in the quivers, resembling the rays of the sun, it shone like Bhogavatī adorned with serpents of blazing visages.

sanskrit: mahārajatavāsobhyām asibhyāṃ ca virājitām rukmabinduvicitrābhyāṃ carmabhyāṃ cāpi śobhitām
english: Illumined by two great silver-hilted swords, and beautified also by two shields variegated with golden studs.

sanskrit: godhāṅgulitrair āsāktaiś citraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ arisaṃghair anādhṛṣyāṃ mṛgaiḥ siṃhaguhām iva
english: With bright finger-guards of iguana hide hung up, adorned with gold, impregnable to hosts of enemies—like a lion's cave to deer.

sanskrit: prāgudaksravaṇāṃ vediṃ viśālāṃ dīptapāvakām dadarśa bharatas tatra puṇyāṃ rāmaniveśane
english: Bharata saw there in Rāma's dwelling a broad and sacred sacrificial altar with its fire blazing, with water flowing toward the northeast.

sanskrit: nirīkṣya sa muhūrtaṃ tu dadarśa bharato gurum uṭaje rāmam āsīnāṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam
english: And having looked about for a moment, Bharata saw his elder—Rāma—seated in the cottage, wearing a coiled mass of matted locks.

sanskrit: taṃ tu kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ cīravalkalavāsasaṃ dadarśa rāmam āsīnam abhitaḥ pāvakopamam
english: He saw Rāma seated there, wearing a black antelope hide and garments of bark and cloth, luminous on every side like fire.

sanskrit: siṃhaskandhaṃ mahābāhuṃ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇam pṛthivyāḥ sagarāntāyā bhartāraṃ dharmacāriṇam
english: With lion's shoulders, mighty arms, eyes resembling the white lotus, righteous in conduct—the lord of the earth bounded by the ocean.

sanskrit: upaviṣṭaṃ mahābāhuṃ brahmāṇam iva śāśvatam sthaṇḍile darbhasasmtīrṇe sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca
english: Seated, the mighty-armed, like the eternal Brahmā, on a ground strewn with darbha grass, together with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bharataḥ śrīmān duḥkhamohapariplutaḥ abhyadhāvata dharmātmā bharataḥ kaikayīsutaḥ
english: Seeing him, the illustrious Bharata, righteous in soul, the son of Kaikeyī, overwhelmed by grief and bewilderment, rushed forward.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca vilalāpārto bāṣpasaṃdigdhayā girā aśaknuvan dhārayituṃ dhairyād vacanam abravīt
english: And seeing him, he lamented in distress; with a voice choked by tears, unable to contain himself through any steadiness, he spoke these words.

sanskrit: yaḥ saṃsadi prakṛtibhir bhaved yukta upāsitum vanyair mṛgair upāsīnaḥ so 'yam āste mamāgrajaḥ
english: "He who should be attended in the assembly by his subjects—that very elder brother of mine now sits attended by forest deer."

sanskrit: vāsobhir bahusāhasrair yo mahātmā purocitaḥ mṛgājine so 'yam iha pravaste dharmam ācaran
english: "That great-souled one who was accustomed to thousands of fine garments—he here wears only an antelope hide, practicing righteousness."

sanskrit: adhārayad yo vividhāś citrāś sumanasas tadā so 'yaṃ jaṭābhāram imaṃ sahate rāghavaḥ katham
english: "He who once wore various splendid and beautiful flowers—how does this Rāghava now endure this burden of matted locks?"

sanskrit: yasya yajñair yathādiṣṭair yukto dharmasya saṃcayaḥ śarīra kleśasaṃbhūtaṃ sa dharmaṃ parimārgate
english: "He whose accumulation of merit was joined through sacrifices performed as prescribed—that same one now pursues righteousness through the mortification born of bodily hardship."

sanskrit: candanena mahārheṇa yasyāṅgam upasevitam malena tasyāṅgam idaṃ katham āryasya sevyate
english: "His body was anointed with precious sandalwood—how is this noble one's body now served by nothing but grime?"

sanskrit: mannimittam idaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpto rāmaḥ sukhocitaḥ dhig jīvitaṃ nṛśaṃsasya mama lokavigarhitam
english: "Rāma, who was born for happiness, has fallen into this suffering on my account. Cursed be the life of cruel me, condemned by all the world!"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vilapan dīnaḥ prasvinnamukhapaṅkajaḥ pādāv aprāpya rāmasya papāta bharato rudan
english: Lamenting thus in his wretchedness, his lotus-face drenched in perspiration, Bharata fell weeping—before he could even reach Rāma's feet.

sanskrit: duḥkhābhitapto bharato rājaputro mahābalaḥ uktvāryeti sakṛd dīnaṃ punar novāca kiṃ cana
english: The mighty prince Bharata, tormented by grief, cried out once pitifully—"O noble one!"—and then could say nothing more.

sanskrit: bāṣpāpihita kaṇṭhaś ca prekṣya rāmaṃ yaśasvinam āryety evābhisaṃkruśya vyāhartuṃ nāśakat tataḥ
english: His throat stopped up with tears, gazing upon the illustrious Rāma, he cried out only "O noble one!" and after that was unable to speak at all.

sanskrit: śatrughnaś cāpi rāmasya vavande caraṇau rudan tāv ubhau sa samāliṅgya rāmo 'py aśrūṇy avartayat
english: Śatrughna too, weeping, bowed at Rāma's feet. Rāma, embracing both of them, himself shed tears.

sanskrit: tataḥ sumantreṇa guhena caiva samīyatū rājasutāv araṇye divākaraś caiva niśākaraś ca yathāmbare śukrabṛhaspatibhyām
english: Then the two princes in that forest were joined by Sumantra and by Guha—as the sun and moon in the sky are joined by Venus and Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: tān pārthivān vāraṇayūthapābhān samāgatāṃs tatra mahaty araṇye vanaukasas te 'pi samīkṣya sarve 'py aśrūṇy amuñcan pravihāya harṣam
english: Seeing those princes gathered there in the great forest, mighty as leaders of elephant herds, the forest-dwellers too all shed tears, casting aside their joy.
